mechanism_narrative: The four-week monotone improvement in RETAIL_REC (-71.4 to -65.4) is driven by recovering discretionary trips that move with transit volumes; as TRANSIT keeps climbing from -63.9 toward -60.6, additional foot traffic reaches retail corridors and lifts the next 28-day mean above the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -71.4 at t-3w to -65.4 at t-0w
fact:TRANSIT rose from -63.9 at t-3w to -60.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to the last 28-day mean while TRANSIT continues to improve week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: Transit use acts as a revealed-safety threshold: only once the TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -60 percent of baseline do households resume non-essential in-store shopping, so the retail rebound accelerates within two weeks of that crossing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -60 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at t-0w is -60.6, within 1 point of the -60 threshold
failure_condition: In the two weeks after TRANSIT crosses above -60, RETAIL_REC falls or stays flat relative to its value at the crossing week.

mechanism_narrative: Retail recovery requires both a release of home time and a normalisation of routine errands: when RESIDENTIAL drops below 16.5 while GROCERY_PHARM simultaneously improves, households chain errands into retail trips, raising RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 16.5 while GROCERY_PHARM rises week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 17.4 at t-3w to 16.7 at t-0w
fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -31.4 at t-1w to -28.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: Weeks where RESIDENTIAL is below 16.5 and GROCERY_PHARM rises are followed by RETAIL_REC means at or below the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Restriction-easing that permits more workplace presence propagates to retail through lunchtime and after-work spending: each week-on-week gain in WORKPLACES above one point pulls RETAIL_REC up over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean improves by more than 1 point week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES is -53.0 at t-0w versus -53.1 at t-3w, essentially flat
regime_hint: restriction-easing phase without renewed stay-at-home orders
failure_condition: A week-on-week WORKPLACES gain above 1 point is followed within four weeks by a 28-day RETAIL_REC mean below the pre-gain 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-summer heat suppresses outdoor activity, so the PARKS series drifting down from -26.0 to -29.3 reallocates leisure hours into air-conditioned indoor venues, producing a short-horizon lift in RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -26.0 at t-3w to -29.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: Weeks with a declining PARKS mean are followed by RETAIL_REC declines of equal or greater magnitude, indicating outdoor and indoor activity move together.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent work-from-home behaviour caps the retail ceiling: while RESIDENTIAL stays above 16.0 and WORKPLACES remains near -53, the retail rebound is concentrated in grocery-anchored trips and mean RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks will be lower than the last four-week mean once the initial reopening bounce decays.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean stays above 16.0 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has been in a 16.0-17.4 band for four weeks
failure_condition: With RESIDENTIAL above 16.0 for two consecutive weeks, the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean exceeds the last 28-day mean by more than 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained transit recovery is the binding constraint on retail capacity because it proxies both permitted trip volume and reopen capacity limits; a two-consecutive-week TRANSIT improvement above two points precedes a four-week RETAIL_REC gain as capacity limits are relaxed in step.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean improves by more than 2 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 3.3 points from t-3w to t-0w
regime_hint: reopening under a phased capacity-limit schedule
failure_condition: Two consecutive TRANSIT gains above 2 points are followed by a 28-day RETAIL_REC mean at or below the pre-gain 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT frozen below -60 while PARKS oscillates without trend indicates a stalled discretionary-mobility regime in which the retail improvement from -71.4 to -65.4 is a low-base artefact of essential trips; absent a transit break-out, RETAIL_REC mean over the next two weeks reverts below the last 28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean remains below -58 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has not exceeded -60.6 over the four observed weeks
failure_condition: While TRANSIT stays below -58 for two consecutive weeks, the following 14-day RETAIL_REC mean rises above the last 28-day mean.
